newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayernverein sees 96 profit up over 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bayernverein sees 96 profit up over 10 pct.

text.p: Bayerische Vereinsbank AG on Friday predicted its earnings would grow by more than 10 percent in 1996 after reporting a 17.5 percent rise in operating profit in the first nine months.
"Chief executive Albrecht Schmidt expects double-digit percentage growth for the full year," Germany's fourth-largest commercial bank said in a statement released ahead of a news conference.
Group operating profit after risk provisions rose to 1.0 billion marks in the nine months to September 30 from 872.6 million marks in the year-earlier period, the bank said.
That was well within the range of analysts' forecasts but represented a clear slowdown from the half-year stage, when operating profit had risen 24 percent.
The bank said in its outlook shareholders should benefit from the expected full-year earnings growth.

It added that it had to contend with a "difficult basis effect" during the second half of the year, because year-on-year earnings growth was being squeezed by the comparison with a strong second half of 1995.
Bayernverein's shares responded by falling 0.40 marks to 55.85 marks in pre-bourse trade.

The slowdown in own-account trading profit growth was particularly marked, with the bank posting a rise of just four percent to 189.8 million marks, below the level of 191.8 million marks posted after the first six months.

Risk provisions were up 17.1 percent at 580.6 million marks after having risen 12.9 percent in the first half. The bank said that the risk profile of its lending portfolio had not improved much despite the slight economic upturn and the absence of major loan defaults.
Net interest income was the driving force behind the earnings growth, rising 7.7 percent to 3.4 billion marks due mainly to strong growth in mortgage lending, the bank said.
Net commission income rose 16.4 percent to 885.9 million marks as a result of buoyant share and bond markets, it said.
Bayernverein's share price has risen sharply in recent months after the disclosure by giant rival Deutsche Bank AG that it had amassed a 5.21 percent stake in the bank.
Bayernverein's interim report made no comment on the stake except to say that Deutsche's announcement had contributed to the share price rise.
Bayernverein's official line has been to welcome Deutsche as a new shareholder but to remain silent on speculation that it may become a takeover target.
